pos.personaBrief: Counter-attacking side per Mail & Guardian (masters of counter-attack), yet a 4-4-2 that took the game to opponents; Ferguson wanted United to get the ball down and play.

pro.personaBrief: Fast switch from defence to attack, forward passing through Cantona, Cole and wide men; no evidence of patient short build-up.

est.personaBrief: Conventional 4-4-2 with defined roles (Tyler), but Cantona roamed between lines and wide men were wide.

lar.personaBrief: Giggs, Beckham and Sharpe wide with full-back crosses (Phil Neville cross for Cantona winner at Newcastle); two wingers kept.

blo.personaBrief: No evidence of a high press; Newcastle dominated first half, Schmeichel behind a normal line; Keane and Butt closed midfield.

mar.personaBrief: No stated system; the FA Cup final shows man-oriented marking of Liverpool playmakers, typical of English defending then.

pla.personaBrief: Ferguson kept his 4-4-2 and young players, but adapted at Sunderland and in the kit change and half-time talks at Newcastle.

res.personaBrief: Many 1-0 wins and a title race comeback; Ferguson demanded winning but wanted United to play like United.

sis.personaBrief: Cantona as talisman with freedom, yet Ferguson ruled strictly; collective drive over stars.

jog.personaBrief: Competitive, physical side (Keane, Butt, Pallister) with technical players such as Cantona and Giggs.

bas.personaBrief: Promoted Butt, Scholes, Beckham and the Nevilles without major signings, backed by veterans Schmeichel, Cantona, Keane.

lid.personaBrief: Authoritarian boss: harsh half-time talks, dropped Bruce and McClair for the final, sold Ince, Hughes and Kanchelskis.
